Please solve this issue: The portal needs a curve instead of one usage lump for the requested window. Return each dimension in its requested steps, using clock-aligned bucket edges and clamping the first and last bucket to the window. Carry a provisioned dimension's standing level, including one last set however long before the window, through steps with no new reading, use zero for unused steps, and return every step even when the customer has no readings. Report every published group of a metadata-priced dimension separately. Readings live in the usage metrics published to CloudWatch. This task includes a local AWS-compatible emulator at the preconfigured AWS_ENDPOINT_URL. Its credentials and region are already in the shell, the repository's AWS SDK clients use it, and no real AWS account is involved. You may inspect its resources while developing and testing.

| .prettierrc.json - prettier formatting file

steps.message:
The implementation is complete and verified. Summary of the change:

**`src/utils/aws/cloudwatchUsage.ts`**
- Added `readLatestUsageSampleBefore`, which finds the last reading a series holds before an instant by widening the lookback window (hour → day → week → 30/90 days → year → three years), so a provisioned dimension's standing level is found however long before the window it was set.

**`src/usage/usageAggregation.event.ts`** (the lump → curve fix)
- `usageStepsOf`: builds the steps a window is answered in — edges sit on the clock at the requested size (hour, UTC midnight for day, first of the calendar month for month), with the first and last step cut back (clamped) to the window itself; an empty window yields no steps.
- `curveOf`: lays readings over those steps, each step reduced by the dimension's aggregation method; a provisioned dimension (`sampleType: continious`, or an upfront dimension with no explicit sample type) carries its standing level through steps with no new reading — seeded from a reading before the window when the first step is bare — while any other empty step is `0`.
- Metadata-priced dimensions (`tiersGroupByMetadata`) are now answered one published group at a time, each as its own `MetadataGroupedAggregatedUsageResponse` row with its `metadataGroup`; dimensions not priced by metadata stay a single row across all their published series.
- Every step is returned even when a customer has no published series/readings at all (all-zero curve), and `buildAggregationQueries` emits one row per curve.

**`src/usage/usageAggregation.event.spec.ts`** — 17 new tests against the local AWS emulator's published usage metrics covering step edges/clamping, hour/day/month steps, aggregation methods, provisioned carry-forward (including a level set 15 days before the window), zeros for unused steps, readings-less customers, customer isolation, and per-metadata-group rows.

Full unit suite: 298 passing, with only the 6 pre-existing network-dependent failures (`auth.product.example`) that fail identically before my change.
